title: Titles Mama Nita and Stratford Hunch
summary: Carew explains Mama Nita as Spanish for little mama and guesses at Stratford Hunch.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yeah. But there's a lot of things that are on here. Well, what is the significance of the tune Mama Mita? Was that...?
Mama Mita? Is it down there as Mama Mita?
Yeah, the first one, Mama Mita. M as in Mike, I-T-A.

There's something you can talk about on that in my estimation. I don't think it's Mama Mita, or should have been. I think it should have been Mama Nita, which is Spanish for little mama. See? Mama Nita. And I think at that time he was going with a Gonzales woman.
Yes, Anita. And he said, Mama Anita. Either Mama Anita or Mama Nita. See? Which means little mama.
Well, how about Stratford Hunch? Does that mean anything at all? Stratford?
Well, I think that was a Chicago dance, but I'm not too positive about that. Oh, it could have been, yeah. I don't see the hunch. You know the funny thing?

He had so many titles. For instance, this Fishtail Blues. Yeah. That was actually the same tune as, what is it, Smokehouse? Something like that, yes. That's right. I like some of these titles. Well, here's one he's got then. I wonder if he had to have somebody in mind. Fickle Faye Creep. Yeah. Somebody to care for. I'll tell you that, some white fella.
Yeah, he sure didn't care for him.
